title: Choose Hestia's look
question: One screen with two lanes: new auction deals by score, and your pipeline. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Bandit Sign
options.lineage: "We Buy Houses" corrugated yard signs on South Florida corners
options.thesis: The wholesaler's own street sign: the score is lettered big enough to read from a car.
options.viewport: Yellow top bar with counts and Collect; a dense ranked table of new deals with the score lettered large; a gray pipeline lane on the right.
options.risk: Reads cheap or shouty if the lettering spreads past the score and the top bar.

raised.raise: Every number is set in tabular figures at table density; the sign never loosens the table.
Yellow owns whole regions, the top bar and the selected deal, never sprinkled as accents.
No card boxes: the lettered score itself is the way into a deal.
Every deal keeps the same furniture in the same place: score, sale day, bid, tax roll, one reason.
Score is also drawn by size, so a 6 reads bigger than a 3 before the digit is read.

options.label: Plat Book
options.lineage: County plat books and parcel maps
options.thesis: Deals laid out as lots on a plat page, each labeled with its parcel number.
options.viewport: Blue county rail on the left, a grid of lots in the middle, the records panel on the right.
options.risk: Familiar: map-and-parcel looks are where property tools usually land, and lots fit fewer deals per screen than a table.

options.label: Centre Rail
options.lineage: Annotated reference editions with a centre key rail
options.thesis: New deals and your pipeline as two columns around a rail of scores, with the sources in the margin.
options.viewport: Two columns twinned around a red score rail; the selected deal's source notes hang in the right margin.
options.case: Carries the cited-sources idea best; loses on audience, since a wholesaler does not live in annotated editions.
options.risk: Close to the current serif-on-paper look, so it can read as the old desk restyled.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Deals as a strobing field of bars and numbers.
options.viewport: A barcode field with one deal pulled into focus.
options.case: Loses both: no tie to real estate, and strobing hurts a working list.
options.kept: Tabular numbers at real data density.
options.risk: A costume of a data art piece.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Counties as swelling lobes of flat color.
options.viewport: One county lobe filling the screen.
options.case: Loses both: playful map shapes hide the ranking.
options.risk: Reads as a leisure guide, not a deal desk.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase type and color tiles as the interface.
options.case: Loses both: tiles fit few deals and the panorama hides the pipeline.
options.kept: No chrome: type is the way in.

options.label: Character Roster
options.thesis: Deals as a ranked roster with a one-line note each.
options.viewport: A pastel grid ranked by score.
options.case: Loses both: cute styling fights a money decision.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Deals as stars sized by score.
options.viewport: A star chart of South Florida deals.
options.case: Loses both: a chart hides the addresses and prices you scan.
options.risk: Decorative at the cost of the task.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS deal table with a sidebar and summary cards, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar, four summary numbers, then the deal table.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other real estate tool by design.
